salient_findings: Dull chest pain of 2 hours' duration

key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
History of coronary artery bypass surgery
Ejection fraction of 25%
Biventricular pacemaker placement
Chest pain duration of 2 hours
ECG shows sinus activity at 72 beats/min

Ventricular depolarization preceded by 2 pacing stimuli
Initial troponin negative 2 hours after symptom onset
Cardiac catheterization revealed thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft
Occlusive lesions in proximal obtuse marginal artery

rejected.label: Graft occlusion
rejected.why: Too general, as it does not specify the type of occlusion or the location.

rejected.label: Occlusive lesions in proximal obtuse marginal artery
rejected.why: While present, this finding does not directly explain the acute presentation and ECG changes as well as the thrombotic occlusion of the saphenous vein graft.

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: The presence of thrombotic occlusion and the specific ECG changes point towards a more definitive acute coronary syndrome diagnosis rather than unstable angina alone.
